page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 56 vCPUs mapped to 28 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is equipped with 224 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and PassMark CPU scores all ranking in the top 25%. Memory performance is bifurcated; the PassMark memory score ranks in the top 10% and small-block cached read bandwidth is in the top 25%, whereas large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the middle 50%. Single-core performance, measured via Geekbench and stress-ng single-core tests, is average. Cryptographic operations are highly efficient, supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions.

The c2d-standard-56 offers a balanced resource density for compute-heavy workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. Its qualitative cost efficiency is characterized by a high physical-to-virtual core density and strong multi-threaded execution capabilities, though workloads requiring high single-threaded throughput or massive uncached memory bandwidth may experience performance bottlenecks. This instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation, ray tracing, image processing, database operations, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-optimized instance featuring 56 vCPUs and 224 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 28 physical cores. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides dedicated CPU allocation with hyperthreading enabled but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark results show strong multi-core CPU performance, PassMark memory scores in the top 10%, and strong database and cryptographic execution. However, single-core performance and large-block uncached memory bandwidth remain average. Given its 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high multi-threaded efficiency, the instance is suited for software compilation, ray tracing, database operations, and medium-scale language model text generation.
